description: We spend a third of our lives sleeping. It's not wasted time: sleep cleans the brain, repairs the body and engraves memories.

hero.hook: Sleeping is not about switching off: it is the body's great nocturnal work.

blocks.text: Over a life of 75 years, we sleep close to **25 years**. For a long time, we believed that sleep was just a break. In reality, it is active work, as vital as drinking or eating.
Science does not yet have all the answers to “why” we sleep. But she knows very well what happens when we don't sleep, and what the night silently repairs.
In **1964**, the American student **Randy Gardner** remained **11 days** without sleeping. Hallucinations, paranoia, mind collapse: proof that the brain cannot survive without rest.

blocks.caption: Sleep, essential for the recovery of the brain and body.

blocks.text: In rats, total absence of sleep kills in **2 to 3 weeks**, like starvation. In humans, a rare genetic disease, **Fatal familial insomnia**, also leads to death. On a daily basis, 17 hours of wakefulness is equivalent to a blood alcohol level of **0.5 g/l**. The brain then forces s, short involuntary breaks in consciousness. [[Microsleeps]]
After his record, Randy Gardner slept **14 hours** straight. He woke up able to function, but it took weeks for his sleep to return to a normal pattern.

During sleep, the brain does not stop: it changes modes. The **seahorse**, a key memory structure in the shape of a sea horse, “replays” the day and sends the information to the [[Neocortex]], the outer layer of the brain, for lasting storage. Result: we often learn **20 to 40%** better after a good night's sleep.

Deep sleep also triggers **growth hormone**, which repairs muscles and tissues, and stimulates , signaling molecules of the immune system. Another major discovery: , a cerebral drainage network **ten times** more active at night. It removes waste, including proteins linked to the risk of Alzheimer's. [[Cytokines]] [[The glymphatic system]]
During deep sleep, brain cells shrink by approximately **60%**. The space thus created allows the cleaning liquid to circulate better.

sections.title: At night, the brain cleans up

blocks.text: Cats sleep **12 to 4 p.m.**: predators safe. Giraffes are sometimes content with **30 minutes to 2 hours**, in short naps, ready to flee. Dolphins sleep with **a single hemisphere**, one half of the brain, at a time, to keep coming up to breathe.
Babies sleep until **6 p.m.**, with a lot of , the phase of dreams with rapid eye movements. This phase helps , the making of connections between neurons. [[paradoxical sleep]] [[Synaptogenesis]]

sections.title: Who sleeps how much, and how

blocks.text: Two forces push us to bed: fatigue which accumulates during the day, and , the internal clock set to **24 hours**. When the light dims, the brain releases **melatonin**, a hormone that prepares the body for sleep without imposing it. [[Circadian rhythms and melatonin]]

Screens in the evening fool this clock and delay falling asleep. We don't really "make up for" a sleep debt on the weekend: fatigue decreases, but not all the damage. Regular hours, a dark and cool room remain the best allies.
Sleep cleanses the brain, repairs the body and strengthens memory. Total deprivation kills in a few weeks: sleeping is not a luxury, it is vital maintenance.
